name: HOLLOW CENTURY: Lives of the Collapse
description: An indie neural sim developed by the Setagaya-Abara Collective that immerses players in procedurally generated lives set during the 2040-2080 Collapse era — hunger, displacement, the slow death of nation-states, and the first emergence of corponation sovereignty. Unlike sanitized historical products, HOLLOW CENTURY uses unfiltered archival emotional data sourced from pre-Meridian memory banks, delivering sensory experiences of grief, scarcity, and radical hope that players describe as 'the most honest thing I've ever felt.' Sessions run up to 72 hours of simulated life.
story_hooks: A player emerges from a 72-hour session convinced they have recovered a genuine ancestral memory containing the location of a pre-Collapse asset cache.
The Setagaya-Abara Collective is offered a buyout by a corponation that wants to 'preserve and curate' the archival emotional data — and bury the rest.
A Tier 4 historian secretly funds the Collective while publicly calling for its shutdown, using the game to research a book that could destabilize corponation founding myths.
